item_shape.data: object, keyed BY CASE TYPE NAME (e.g. Functional, Performance, Other, Security, Acceptance, Accessibility, Usability, Compatibility, ..., Automated, Manual, Total) — NOT an array, and NOT positional. Matches schema.
item_shape.data.<Type>.graphData: object keyed by 3-letter month abbreviation (Jan..Dec) -> integer count. NOT a positional array. Matches schema.
item_shape.data.<Type>.field: string, present on every real case-type/automation-state entry (e.g. 'case_type', 'automation_state') EXCEPT Total, which omits it entirely
item_shape.data.<Type>.value: array of strings on real entries (e.g. ["9379"]); on Total it is [null] instead
item_shape.order: array of the same keys as data, giving display sequence

contract.json_path: data.<Type>.field (nested required, per schema: data.<Type> requires [graphData, field, value])

notes:
PREPROD ASSUMPTION CHECK: the task briefing's framing ('positional-array bug') does NOT apply to this capability. describeCapability's declared schema explicitly types data as an object map (properties keyed by case-type name, e.g. Accessibility, Functional, Acceptance, ... Automated, Manual, Total) and each entry's graphData as an object keyed by 3-letter month abbreviations (Jun..May) -- never an array. This is unlike the sibling capabilities get_issues_count_info / get_closed_test_runs_info, which declare positional arrays but actually return objects (a schema-vs-reality contradiction). Here schema and guidance both correctly describe the object/map shape, and prod's live response on project 332537 (16,267 cases) confirms it exactly: data is a map of ~45 case-type/automation-state keys (real types plus several stray custom types with all-zero series, e.g. '8may-1', 'analytical', 'dummy_test'), each with graphData as a month-keyed object (Oct..Sep, real non-trivial counts e.g. Functional Sep=16445, Manual Sep=26476, Total Sep=26594), and order lists the same ~45 keys. So: object-map shape is CONFIRMED on prod with real volume, not positional-array -- no drift on that axis.

THE ACTUAL DRIFT: schema declares 'field' as required for every entry under data (required: [graphData, field, value] on each data.<Type> object, no exception carved out for Total). The live prod response's Total entry is {graphData: {...}, value: [null]} -- it omits 'field' entirely, exactly as preprod found. Total.value is [null] (not an array of strings) on prod too, same as preprod, though per the shallowest-missing-path convention only the missing 'field' key is flagged as the reportable contract violation. Guidance says 'Total is a sibling key... the CSV exporter special-cases it' but the schema's required-list is never relaxed for it, so this is a genuine declared-vs-actual mismatch, now reproduced with real data volume (16,267 cases, 12-month trailing window Oct-Sep, all real integer counts) instead of preprod's ~21-case near-empty fixture. Verdict: DRIFT, driven solely by data.Total missing the required 'field' key (and Total.value's null-in-array typing); the map/graphData shape itself is a PASS against schema.
